title: S3 clock-skew 403 arrives as generic PermissionError; classify by message in shared transient list
answers: S3OperationError reported to error tracking for RequestTimeTooSkewed
delete_folder clock skew PermissionError shows up as a bug in data import sync
How to make a new S3 transient error retried in warehouse pipeline
body:
Symptom: A warehouse/data-import sync's best-effort cleanup of an old query folder creates an error-tracking issue (S3OperationError) even though the sync is fine; the underlying S3 error is a clock-skew rejection.
Root cause: s3fs maps every 403 (including RequestTimeTooSkewed) onto a generic PermissionError, so only the fixed message text distinguishes it. `delete_folder` in products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/util.py only skipped capture for `_is_transient_s3_connection_error`, and `TRANSIENT_OBJECT_STORE_ERRORS` in pipelines/core/delta/errors.py lacked the message.
Fix pattern: add the S3 fixed message substring to `TRANSIENT_OBJECT_STORE_ERRORS` (used by `is_transient_object_store_error`) and widen the `delete_folder` capture guard to `_is_transient_s3_connection_error(e) or is_transient_object_store_error(e)`.
Constraints: Only for errors that self-clear on retry and have a stable S3 message. Do not classify bare PermissionError as transient; real AccessDenied must still be captured. Add a case to `TestIsTransientObjectStoreError` and a `delete_folder` test in tests/test_util.py.
applies: Warehouse sources data-import pipeline S3/delta error classification
